question: Your team shares a boilerplate-generation skill in .claude/skills/ that needs a target module name to create a new service scaffold. Engineers often invoke the skill without any arguments, and the agent then guesses a module name or produces generic placeholder code. What is the most effective way to make sure engineers supply the required module name?

options.text: Add context: fork to the skill's SKILL.md frontmatter so the skill runs in an isolated sub-agent context.
options.reason: context: fork isolates verbose or exploratory skill output from the main session; it does not prompt engineers for a missing parameter.

options.text: Move the scaffold instructions from the skill into the project CLAUDE.md file so they are always loaded in every session.
options.reason: CLAUDE.md holds always-loaded universal standards, while skills fit on-demand task workflows; moving the instructions does not prompt engineers for the module name.

options.text: Set allowed-tools in the skill's SKILL.md frontmatter to permit only the Write tool during skill execution.
options.reason: allowed-tools restricts which tools the skill may use, for example to prevent destructive actions; it does not ask engineers for required arguments.

options.text: Add an argument-hint field to the skill's SKILL.md frontmatter that describes the required module name parameter.
options.reason: The argument-hint frontmatter option prompts developers for required parameters when they invoke the skill without arguments, so engineers supply the module name.
